MATTHEVV.|39}}</noinclude>and it vvas giuen to the damsel, and she brought it to her mother. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=12}}† And his Disciples came and tooke the body, and ‖ buried it: {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ S. Iohns disciples at this time had wel learned their duety toward Christ.}}∷ and came and told IESVS.

{{verse|chapter=14|verse=13}}† Which vvhen IESVS had heard, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 6, 31. Lu. 9, 10. Io. 6, 2.''}}* he ‖ retired from thence by boate, into a desert place apart, and the multitudes hauing heard of it, folovved him on foote out of the cities. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=14}}† And he coming forth savv a great multitude, and pitied them, and cured their diseased. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=15}}† And vvhen it vvas euening, his Disciples came vnto him, saying, It is a desert place, and the houre is novv past: dimisse the multitudes that going into the tovvnes, they may bye them selues victuals. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=16}}† But IESVS said to them, They haue no neede to goe: giue ye them to eate. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=17}}† They ansvvered him. We haue not here, but fiue loaues, and tvvo fishes. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=18}}† Who said to them, Bring them hither to me. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=19}}† And vvhen he had commaunded the multitude to sitte dovvne vpon the grasse, he tooke the fiue loaues and the two fishes, and looking vp vnto heauen he blessed and brake, and gaue the loaues to his Disciples, and ‖ the Disciples to the multitudes. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=20}}† And they did al eate, and had their fil. And they tooke the leauings, twelue ful baskettes of the fragments. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=21}}† And the number of them that did eate vvas, fiue thousand men, beside vvomen and children.

{{verse|chapter=14|verse=22}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpon the Octaue of S. Peter and S. Paul. Iulij 6.}}And forth vvith IESVS commaunded his Disciples to goe vp into the boate, and to goe before him ouer the vvater, til he dimissed the multitudes. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=23}}† And hauing dimissed the multitude, he {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 6, 46. Io. 6, 16.''}}* ascended into a mountaine alone to praye. And vvhen it vvas euening, he vvas there alone. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=24}}† But the boate in the middes of the sea vvas tossed vvith vvaues. for the vvinde vvas contrarie. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=25}}† And in the fourth vvatch of the night, he came vnto them vvalking vpon the sea. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=26}}† And seeing him vpon the ‖ sea vvalking, they vvere troubled saying, That it is a ghost. and for feare they cried out. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=27}}† And immediatly IESVS spake vnto them, saying, Haue confidence: it is I, feare ye not. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=28}}† And Peter making ansvver said, Lord if it be thou, bid me come to thee vpon the vvaters. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=29}}† And he said, Come. And Peter descending out of the boate, ‖ vvalked vpon the vvater to come to IESVS. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=30}}† But seeing the vvinde rough, he vvas afraid: and vvhen he began to be drovvned, he cried out saying, Lord, saue me. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=31}}† And incontinent {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Notwithstanding the infirmities of them that gouerne the Churche, yet Christ sustaineth them, and holdeth them vp, yea and by them, whatsoeuer they are, he vpholdeth and preserueth his Church.}}∷ IESVS stretching forth his hand tooke hold of him, and said vnto him, O thou of litle faith, vvhy didst thou doubt? {{verse|chapter=14|verse=32}}† And vvhen<noinclude>{{rh|||they}}</noinclude>
